Complete authentication and session security checks
notes: Found a user-enumeration TIMING oracle in api/auth/login: `user?.active ? verifyPassword(...) : false` short-circuits, so an unknown email AND a deactivated account skipped scrypt entirely despite DUMMY_HASH existing to prevent exactly that. Measured 32.6ms vs 0.0007ms (33000x). Fixed by verifying unconditionally and ANDing `active` separately. Live HTTP proof against the production build: 145ms vs 149ms (0.98x). Also made the 401 message name neither field. scripts/test-auth-security.ts 30/30, 4/4 mutants killed. Preserved XT_TRUST_PROXY opt-in, login CSRF exemption, refresh rotation and TTLs.

title: Complete origin and CSRF negative tests

Complete rate-limit and abuse controls
notes: 9 state-changing routes had NO rate limit: users, users/[id], nodes, nodes/[id], port-forwards, port-forwards/[id], tunnels/[id] DELETE, tunnels/[id]/logs POST, webhooks, webhooks/[id]. POST /api/users runs scrypt hashPassword (~100ms) per call, so an authenticated ADMIN could saturate a 1 vCPU core. All buckets keyed on auth.user.id and placed AFTER requireSession. scripts/test-rate-limit.ts 30/30 incl. live 429 (statuses 201,429) and a build-staleness guard. 4/4 mutants killed with a rebuild each -- the first run's 1/4 was stale-build methodology, not a suite gap. Not a distributed limiter: buckets are per-process and in-memory, as documented.
